title: Totally ramified base change
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of complete DVRs with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$, and suppose $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $K_1/K$ be finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $A_1$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Suppose $A_1/\mathfrak m_{A_1}=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_AA_1=\mathfrak m_{A_1}^{[K_1:K]}$ (total ramification). Then $L\otimes_KK_1$ is a field, $B\otimes_AA_1$ is its integral closure of $B$ and is a complete DVR, and $\mathfrak m_{A_1}(B\otimes_AA_1)=\mathfrak m_{B\otimes_AA_1}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The residue field of $B\otimes_AA_1$ is the residue field of $B$. Local means pulling back maximal ideals, and finite means finite-dimensional.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified; completeness is a harmless strengthening of its hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $n=[K_1:K]\geq1$. The DVR $A$ is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]; being local and complete, it is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata]. Applying [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] at the prime $(0)$ and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] to the finite extension $K_1/K$, $A_1$ is a finite $A$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $A_1$ is a domain with fraction field $K_1$. The domain clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] makes $A_1$ local. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $A$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension $1$, so [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] (with $D=A$, $C=A_1$) gives a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A_1$ over $\mathfrak m_A$, maximal, with $(A_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ a DVR and $\mathfrak m_{(A_1)_{\mathfrak q}}\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$. As $A_1$ is local, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_{A_1}$ and every element outside $\mathfrak q$ is already a unit, so $(A_1)_{\mathfrak q}=A_1$: thus $A_1$ is a DVR and $A\to A_1$ is local. Choose uniformizers $\pi\in A$ and $t\in A_1$. Apply [lem-sfb-totally-ramified-uniformizer-presentation] using the given residue-field isomorphism and $\mathfrak m_AA_1=\mathfrak m_{A_1}^n$. It gives $A_1=A[T]/(P)$ and $K_1=K[T]/(P)$ under $T\mapsto t$, with $P=T^n+\sum_{i<n}a_iT^i$, $a_i\in\pi A$ and $a_0=\pi u$ for $u\in A^\times$.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: choice of uniformizers and the Eisenstein presentation; finiteness, locality and DVR property of A_1 via Algebra Tags 032W, 0325 and the finite-normalization localization (More on Algebra 09EM (1))

proof.text: The equality $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ says that the image of $\pi$ generates $\mathfrak m_B$, so it is a uniformizer of $B$. The image of $u$ is a unit. In a DVR a uniformizer times a unit is not in the square of its maximal ideal: cancellation from $\pi u=\pi^2b$ would make $\pi$ a unit. Thus the image $P_B\in B[T]$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-eisenstein-quotient-dvr]. Consequently $C=B[T]/(P_B)$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $(x)$, where $x$ is the class of $T$.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: P remains Eisenstein because pi is a uniformizer of B

proof.text: There is a canonical $B$-algebra isomorphism $B\otimes_AA_1\cong C$: it sends $b\otimes q(t)$ to $bq(x)$; its inverse sends constants $b$ to $b\otimes1$ and $x$ to $1\otimes t$. The polynomial relation makes both maps well-defined, and they are inverse on constants and the generator. The same formulas over $K\to L$ identify $L\otimes_KK_1$ with $L[T]/(P_L)=C[1/\pi]$, since every nonzero denominator in $B$ is a unit times a power of $\pi$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], so $B[1/\pi]=L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] this localization has dimension $n$ over $L$. It is a nonzero domain because $C$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$ in $C$ (the monic quotient basis makes $B\to C$ injective). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] makes it a field $L_1$. Since it contains $C$ and consists of fractions of $C$, it is $\operatorname{Frac}(C)$.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: tensor presentations and the asserted field L_1; the fraction-field identification is written out

proof.text: The residue quotient is $C/(x)=B[T]/(P_B,T)=B/(a_0)=B/(\pi)$, with the constant map giving the isomorphism. Thus $\mathfrak m_C\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$, and $B\to C\subset L_1$ is local. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $C$ is a finite $B$-module; $B$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], local and complete, and $C$ is a domain, so the domain clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] shows that $C$ is complete for its maximal ideal. $C$ is integral over $B$ (finite) and lies in $L_1=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ (Step 3). Conversely, an element of $L_1$ integral over $B$ is integral over $C\supseteq B$, and $C$ is normal as a principal ideal domain [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], so it lies in $C$. Hence $C$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $L_1$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Finally $\mathfrak m_{A_1}=(t)$ and the tensor presentation sends $t$ to $x$, so $\mathfrak m_{A_1}C=(x)=\mathfrak m_C$. The residue quotient above is the claimed unchanged residue field.
